I enjoy it more than the first game, which I found very difficult to get very far in. I like the wider focus, and the way the game introduces the gameplay mechanic with many tutorials made it easy to understand how everything works.

Graphics are great, atmosphere is heavy, and there is a darkly comedic vein running through it all. I call it a Misery Simulator, and I love it.

Not exactly a 'sequel' to the first game, but still an incredible game. Although, The price for the game is a little steep, I'd recommend getting it for <$30.
Graphics are really good, runs decently well, and the gameplay is also quite fun. Keep in mind, this game is ridiculously difficult and will require some learning.
So buggy on Mac, it consistently crashes even trying to load an early-game save. Unplayable.

The U.I. is very clunky, and very unintuitive for a first-time play-through. Even on the easiest difficulty, the faction system is aggressively annoying. The idea of factions is pretty neat, but the execution is rather clunky. The modding scene also leaves much to be desired. The modding tool, Frostkit, is listed as requiring nearly 100 GB in storage space on the Epic Games Store, which is rather ridiculous.

Much of the conceptual work for this game is quite amazing, in my opinion. There are a lot of good ideas. I like the research system and the law and council system, but the U.I. is overbearing for all at times. I personally do not like the resource system in this game. Playing on endless, it felt like I ran out of coal instantly, and had no time to adjust production / extraction to remedy that problem while having to also deal with constant protests over ONE law change, and balance the need for consumer goods, prefabs, heatstamps, etc.

Pertaining to protests and law, my session on the easiest difficulty, felt a little too realistic lmao.

Edit:

Yeah the core mechanics of the game do not play like I expected in the slightest. For me, this is a no.

A true sequel in every sense. A worthy continuation of the original game's story. A logical expansion of the lore through the game mechanics: from building a small city building by building in the first game, to becoming the architect of a sprawling ice-bound metropolis in the second game. Some people disliked this game for not being a carbon copy of the first game, but what would be the point of that? This was a bold and creative decision by 11 bit studios to make something new and progressive in the stagnating games industry. We should celebrate them for that brave initiative, and we should celebrate this excellent game. Gorgeously melancholic in the theme of the original Frostpunk, with wondrous, heart-aching music, and stunning visuals.

Love it so far. The goal of the game is about being a "good" political leader which is quite confounding. It is a good replication of the real world democracy. With the gorgeous frozen world and post apocalyptic atmosphere, Pretty sure I am going to put more hours in it.

I was so excited to see the sequel, and after playing it for 17 hours so far, I'm not disappointed. It's just as challenging with its bigger scale, I've restarted several times to make my city more efficient. I like that we're managing a growing community - multiple communities at that, and I appreciate the thought that went into this.
Endless mode just keeps freezing, cant even load a save anymore. Dont buy until they fix all this shit.

fun game. lots of mechanics. very different from FP1, but still fun. can be challenging for newer players because of the factions/politics system. great dynamic play, but you have to sit down and make a few mistakes to learn how to drive it.
Too little content. Very disappointing how quickly i finished this game compared to frostpunk 1

Not really sure what's going on after completing the tutorial, so trying to do the basics like housing, food and coal is impossible because I need heatstamps? Can't get those cause I need more materials but can't get those cause I need more heatstamps? Why didn't the tutorial use that word at all or let me know how to create/balance them? Why don't my people harvest things? I have to build something to harvest anything?

People die by the hundreds, and nothing bad seems to happen in my city. Hell, I can't even figure out how to make graves or look into making hospitals or medical tents. I passed a few laws, but having kids as apprentices didn't do anything I could notice. I picked what seemed like a nice law, free basics for everyone, and now i have Fatih Keepers trying to go door to door about it? How was I supposed to know that would lead my group into militant faith? So very little information is communicated to you, it took me an hour to learn that frostbreaking actually costs something because it came across as free in the tutorial.

Another great game and an even better follow-up from the original Frostpunk in my opinion.

Still was a bit difficult for me to finish the game even on the easiest mode, but I quite enjoyed the story, the graphics, the tough choices, the epic music, and the bittersweet ending to the campaign.

Honestly, while I still prefer the 1st game for its heavy atmosphere and resource management mechanics, I'm very glad Frostpunk 2 exists. While it doesn't really mirror the 1st game gameplay-wise, the grim hopelessness is replaced by an industrial macabre. You aren't fighting cold, you are fighting political instability. While Frostpunk 2 as a game may be missing some of the intricacies that made its' predecessor so great, I am very excited to see what the DLC has in store, especially given the gem that was The Last Autumn.

This game is excellent - do not listen to the 2-hours-on-record reviewers who expected the same game as last time, with a new skin. This is how you make a sequel - you push the concept in a new and exciting direction while maintaining the spirit and feel of the old game! This is an excellent and deep city buidling, reminding me of the early days of the genre in the 90's. Yes, there is a deep political system to understand, but once you do, the system does a great work at puting the different factions in your city at odds with each other, with you trying to minimize the damage....or just taking outright control. Some people have complained about that the placement of buildings doesnt matter, that the game is simple to beat without spending time with careful placement. There is a solution to that, obviously...increase the difficulty. I have tried the highest difficulty, and trust me, at that point every single decision and buidling has to be very thought through.

11/10, would incarcerate, sterilize and exile the opposition again.

Very entertaining city builder and I have had a lot of fun with this series. Lots of unique systems and ideas, societal choices and skill trees, fun mechanics and fun game overall. It is a depressing story, but man is it a fun series. Played all the content of the 1st one and definitely led me to buy the second. As a RTS\City builder enjoyer, this game is DIFFICULT. I spent hours restarting campaigns due to subtle mistakes on easy mode. Custom matches are an option where you can change your resources on the map (recommended for sure). No Paywall bullshit. Once you buy the game and its content, you got all of it. No in game currency exchange or added bonuses you have to shell out more dollars for. I paid full price for both and its been worth it to me. I am excited for the coming DLC.

Held off buying this game for years because of the mixed review, after finally playing it I can say I have no idea why it has mixed reviews. This game is an awesome sequel to the first frostpunk, intoducing the same intense nail biting experience and expanding on the first game's already amazing morality system.

I somehow played for 50 hours and now I don’t want to return to this game at all. It didn’t stick, didn’t leave an impression, didn’t captivate me at all, completely different from how it was with Frostpunk 1.

This game has lost the charm of the original. Too many options, menus and submenus. Unlike the original, which I played for hours on end, finding it difficult to put down, I want to quit this one after an hour. Incredibly disappointing.
this game is trash next to the old one, the GUI is worse, Mechanics are worse. building is worse. the game is all around a regret of a purchase.

Hmmm. Unsure about this one. The blatant hate this game gets due to being compared to its strong predecessor is undeserved. The devs went out of their way to actually alter the game enough to justify a second part, while they kept a ton of what the first game made good. For example the many moral decisions you have to take, those are still in here and still cause trouble. A lot of trouble.

Yet I still understand why so many enjoyed the first part more. For me personally this game did never achieve the atmospheric heights of the first one, and especially the first two hours were rough. I almost refunded it at the two hour mark, just not being that entertained playing it? But I am still glad to have pushed through the first hours, it got more interesting later on, especially once the politic system seemed more clear to me.

So yeah... a mixed bag this one. Not really a bad game, yet by far not achieving the heights of its predecessor.
Its fun I prefer the original where i can watch my little guys work but this is a good challenge
This game is hard, but I enjoy the difficulty. Especially the story, the whitouts, and the factions and their demands. Even one the easiest difficulty the game is still a challenge.

This game is very disappointing. FrostPunk was fun, innovative, stressful and interesting. This game is boring, sim-city style city builder where there is very little flexibility in building. It's very slow paced, like an idle game instead of the intense stress of the first game. I pre-ordered this and seriously considered returning it. We can't even see the people trudge paths through the snow like in the first game. Everything is so high level you can't look at any of the fun details of the game.

Not as great as the first game, they really wanted to change the direction of the game for some reason, not always for the better. Whether or not you played the first game, you will probably still enjoy this one. If you absolutely HATE changes then maybe avoid it.
Dont Expect FP1. Its a nice game really worth it but on sale its great value for money.

FP2 is a disappointing game—sad to say.

I played FP1 for 63 hours, bought all the DLCs, and absolutely loved it. The game had an amazing story, engaging mechanics, and impactful decisions. You could feel the cold, the pain, and the struggle of the people. You had to take care of them, make tough choices to survive, and manage the pressure and planning. None of that is present in FP2.

In FP2, you feel nothing. The game is extremely easy, more reminiscent of SimCity 1. It doesn't even feel like a sequel—it's more of a standalone game, and a poor one at that.

I'm very disappointed. After 14 years of using Steam, this is the first time I've requested a refund. It's simply not worth the money.

Main story review, light mechanics spoilers below:

Frostpunk 2 is an excellent follow up to the first game. It takes the first game's base mechanics and scales it up, giving you more to manage and more challenge. There might be some personal stakes/emotion lost in the translation from 400 people towns to 40,000 people towns, but the larger scale opens up so much fun and challenging content that it evens out.

The factions system, in particular, I really enjoyed. It delved deeper into the somewhat shallow politics system from the first game. I enjoy that there's a proper council/congress as well. Overall just an excellent city builder/survival experience. The only thing that sucks is that the soundtrack isn't quite as good as the first game's.

Highly recommend!

9/10

After several updates, I can now confidently change my recommendation from Not Recommended to Recommended. The game has become significantly more stable—crashes and save file issues, which were once major concerns, seem to have been largely resolved. This alone makes a big difference in the overall experience.

That said, there are still a few areas that could be improved.

First, the colony furnace capacity feels too limited in its current state. When managing a large settlement with multiple residential districts and expanded infrastructure, the heating system struggles to keep up. Increasing the furnace capacity would greatly improve late-game balance and make city planning more flexible.

Second, there is noticeable performance lag during temperature changes. As the number of districts and buildings grows, each shift in temperature causes a brief but noticeable freeze. While it no longer leads to crashes, it still disrupts the gameplay flow and immersion.

Overall, Frostpunk 2 is moving in the right direction. The core gameplay remains engaging, and the developers have clearly made progress in addressing critical technical issues. With further optimization and balance adjustments, this could become an even stronger sequel.

I hope 11 bit studios will take these suggestions into consideration.

I can't recommend it enough. This is a great city builder with a huge emphasis on social interactions. Multiple factions supporting multiple vision of what should be your little city-state, balancing resources shortage, angry mob and borderline morals, fighting the unrest with words, praises, promises or armed guards.

Steward, your choices will save the city. Or doom it.

I absolutely love Frostpunk 2. The city-building, political system, atmosphere, soundtrack, and overall gameplay are outstanding. It's one of the most engaging strategy games I've played in a long time

Unfortunately, I can't recommend it right now because of one major issue - the game crashes constantly. Sometimes it crashes after 10-15 minutes, sometimes after an hour, but it happens so often that it completely ruins the experience. Losing progress and having to restart over and over is incredibly frustrating

I really hope the developers focus on fixing the stability issues, because underneath the crashes there's an amazing game that deserves much better.

Please prioritize stability. I want to enjoy this game, but in its current state it's very difficult

if i ignore how insanely good frostpunk 1 is, frostpunk 2 stands really well on its own. it's different from frostpunk 1.

but the musical motifs really hit me hard, so imo i like it. it's not as replayable but its like a movie i really, really enjoyed.

the first run is the most special one of them all, try not to look at spoilers and hope for the best.
Definitely not like the original Frostpunk. This game is on a much larger scale and politics in the game have a huge impact. It's fun I enjoyed it.

I have been waiting for this game for 2 years, and the devs have certainly delivered. I do also very much appreciate the rapid patches which very much helped with game stability and QoL, and the continued support for the game by the studio.

Played some on Game Pass as well. This is an amazing game, and such a good sequel. The first game was about solving the same problems as this one, but focused on micro management. In this one, you solve the same problems, and it has the same grim, steam punk aesthetic, where your decisions feel like they carry weight, but it's more macro oriented this time around. This might be the best sequel to any game I've played, it's advanced the story & the gameplay in a way that makes sense.

There is something with the focus on the endless utopia and faction dynamics, that just don't really work as intended. Frostpunk 1 was such an incredibly well-curated almost failing experience, with each scenario having its own set of challenges to overcome. Frostpunk 2 just never gets close in terms of how tight the gameplay feels. 

I did, however, have at least one run on Utopia mode that did just what Frostpunk 1 managed: I barely survived the first whiteout, total resource depletion, faction conflict, then the plague, then a volcanoe whiteout, and then a whiteout again. It was one crisis after the other, just barely making it through. 

So the game CAN still deliver the real Frostpunk experience. I just never managed to get that dynamic back in any of my other runs, however difficult I tried to make them. I just ended up endlessly having to put one law into place, just to remove it again, to keep my factions from killing each other. And the outposts.. man, the meta is broken in this game. You can just trivialize everything by rushing outposts early. Absolutely not fun, once you know it's possible.

Good but not worth $45 in my opinion. Pretty standard city builder game with some cool thematic elements and interesting decisions to make. Some of the choices are actually conflicting, others are just so black and white in terms of morality that it kind of makes you roll your eyes.

If you are any good at strategy games or city builders you can complete the main campaign in about 15 hours or less. Pretty short game for the price, I'd buy it on sale. Hoping DLC will flesh things out a bit.
